target: simple formula calculator, separate case-study page, and retail-style draft back-label generator

contract.purpose: Turn one submitted manufacturing formula into a traceable composition report with visible assumptions and corrections.
contract.canonicalPurpose: Formula Composition Engine helps food, nutraceutical, supplement, and medicinal-product formulation teams turn one mixed-format batch formula into a reviewable macro, micro, active, preservative, and uncertainty report by combining exact unit-safe calculation with ranked, correctable ingredient identities.
contract.audience: Formulators and product teams reviewing food, nutraceutical, supplement, or medicinal batch formulas.
contract.job: Submit one formula, correct only material ambiguities, export a traceable composition report, and prepare a conventional draft back label from the result.
contract.thesis: The formula is the work surface; uncertainty stays visible in the result and the draft label uses familiar Indian retail hierarchy instead of a novel demographic dashboard.
contract.system: Simple Laboratory Workbench with a monochrome retail-label module: editable serving details beside a printable nutrition panel.
contract.signature: Every incomplete label value remains visibly marked as a lower bound and linked to the calculation's evidence boundary.
contract.risk: A visually expressive evidence system could distract from high-density review; the selected direction must preserve familiar table scanning and keyboard correction.

projectCheck.command: pnpm check && pnpm build && PYTHONPATH=src uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

findings: The owner selected the simple workbench direction and explicitly rejected additional product-shell complexity.
The case-study page reuses the approved workbench system and adds only a two-link header; no new product shell or dependency was added.
Browser checks at 390, 768, and 1440 pixels found 26 product cards, 55 comparison rows, and no horizontal overflow.
Responsive screenshots at 390, 768, and 1440 pixels retain the single-column formula workflow and compact database disclosure.
Formula history and reusable ingredient profiles use the same recovery-key-scoped D1 workspace without adding account navigation.
The owner delegated the label direction and asked for conventions found on actual products; the selected module uses one adult RDA column rather than separate child versions.
The label remains visibly theoretical, marks partial values as lower bounds, and retains the existing regulatory-review boundary.
Responsive label evidence at 390, 768, and 1440 pixels keeps all four nutrition columns visible without horizontal overflow.
The 517.57 kB lazy ingestion chunk remains a build warning; PDF, spreadsheet, and OCR code is loaded only when needed.

ownerFeedback.note: The owner said separate child versions were unnecessary, delegated the direction choice, and asked to follow what is available on actual products.
